evidence_notes: Judged from the eight named PNGs only: four committed plates at 1295x1061 and four 1400x1146 re-renders. No SVG was opened, searched or read.

Plate-to-re-render pairing measured by mean absolute grey difference after resizing both to 518x424: image-1 to the fine plate at 3.19 (against 3.88 for the standard/titan plates and 5.70 for full-axis), image-3 to the CPU-lane standard plate at 3.14, image-5 to the full-axis plate at 3.10, image-7 at 3.14 to both the standard and titan plates.

Red-mark census of each plate found exactly three components at consistent pixel positions: the hollow conductor-only cross at (453,548), the filled solved cross at (927,245) and the filled solved axis triangle at (1006,546). The hollow cross is 25x25 px and 300 red pixels with a white core; the filled cross is 25x25 px and 413 red pixels, solid at the centre; the triangle is 21x22 px and 259 red pixels.

The reviewed run's receipt records the polished vacuum saddle at R = 1.8136 m, Z = 0.00009 m with |grad psi| = 1.4e-16 Wb/m on a converged polish, which matches the position of the hollow cross in every plate.
Border scan of every plate and re-render: 0 non-white pixels on the top, bottom, left and right edges, so no content is clipped by the canvas boundary.

Ink census of the CPU-lane standard plate: 17.6 percent of pixels carry ink; the lavender plasma-cell region is 7.5 percent of the canvas at mean RGB (217,203,236), a pale fill that recedes behind the contours.

The CPU-lane standard plate and the titan-lane plate are visually identical (mean absolute grey difference 0.0, maximum channel difference 12), which is the lane-agreement result rather than a duplicated figure defect.

The evidence caption is substantive, not a restatement of the panel titles: it names the hollow-cross convention, the 4.5 mm Newton polish of the vacuum saddle, the absence of an in-wall O point, the shared 24-level contour array, and the three sibling lane views. It is not a finding.

The reviewed head commit b97b2053d576 regenerated the four SVG siblings and their receipts but left all four PNG plates byte-identical, so the plates judged here are the ones produced at 9d5a6bf92, the last plate-producing commit. Whether the SVG and PNG renderings now differ cannot be judged without opening an SVG, which this review is instructed not to do.

findings.summary: The conductor-only stationary point is drawn hollow and the solved admitted saddle is drawn filled, but the two marks are the same red, the same 25x25 px size and only 474 px apart in adjacent panels, with no legend and no direct label anywhere on either plate. Measured on the committed PNGs: the hollow conductor cross has a white core (its centre 7x7 window carries 4 of 49 red pixels) and the solved cross is solid red (49 of 49), so the distinction exists in the pixels, but at a 900 px column each mark is about 17 px and the fill difference is easy to miss on a figure whose marks carry no key. A reader who lands on the figure through the Figures index, without the evidence caption that explains the hollow convention, cannot tell an unadmitted vacuum candidate from the admitted saddle. Not blocking: the caption does name it and each mark sits in a separately titled panel.

The flux contours are drawn in a hairline pale grey whose solid core measures 153 of 255 (about 2.85:1 against white), with most anti-aliased pixels between 184 and 246 and therefore under 1.6:1. In the outer field, where levels are widely spaced, the curves are faint at page width while the black vessel outline carries far more visual weight than the field the figure exists to show. The field stays readable and no contour is lost, so this is a legibility margin rather than a defect; a heavier contour stroke would put the weight on the data.

The plate is drawn on a 9.2 x 6.4 in canvas (1295 x 1061 px at 200 dpi after tight bounding, aspect 1.22:1) rather than the declared 14 in wide slide canvas, and the panel titles are set at 9 pt. Two side-by-side square poloidal panels justify a tighter canvas and nothing is cramped or clipped, so the plate reads well; a reader placing it beside other figures on the same page will nonetheless notice the different proportional weight.

The axes limits are the data lattice extent, so the outboard and inboard conductor context stops where the grid stops: the pale coil shapes at the top and bottom of each panel terminate mid-structure at the frame edge. The canvas itself is clean (0 non-white pixels on all four edges, so nothing is cut by the image boundary) and the vessel, plasma boundary and all stationary points are complete, so this is framing rather than clipping; it slightly limits how much machine context a reader can see around the solve.
